tldr: Across 10 country buckets, headlines frame the German state elections almost unanimously as a personal crisis for Chancellor Merz and a historic CDU collapse, with AfD's third regional win treated as a direct blow to the governing centre. Most mastheads place Merz — not the AfD or its voters — as the protagonist, asking how he will respond rather than why Germans voted as they did.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use declarative, finality-framed language — 'stability is ending' — absent from every Western masthead, which asks questions or focuses on Merz's response.
Only headline to reach for Cold War and East German historical identity as an explanatory frame for the AfD's rise; all news headlines treat the result as an electoral event, not a historical one.
Only headline to explicitly name the centre as 'floundering' — framing this as a crisis for democratic centrism rather than an AfD win story.
Only headline to introduce an economic explanatory angle ('Will economy shape the vote?'), and the sole pre-election piece positing structural drivers absent from all post-election headline coverage.

bottom_line: Headline coverage makes Merz's political crisis the story, not AfD's voters or structural polarization; no headline in the corpus asks why Germans chose the far-right, only what Merz will do next.
